newsitem.title: USA: Southwest Air on cost-cutting drive.
newsitem.headline: Southwest Air on cost-cutting drive.

text.p: Southwest Airlines Co has launched a company-wide bid to drag down costs after seeing them creep up throughout this year, Chief Financial Officer Gary Kelly said.
"We have a number of very large cost-reduction initiatives underway and are about to step up to an even more intense effort to reduce costs," he said on a conference call.
As part of the effort, he said Southwest will tighten its purchasing practices, consolidate vendors and try to negotiate lower prices from suppliers.
"I think we will have savings online in 1997 in excess of $10 million a year, maybe as high as double that," Kelly said.
Kelly said a new computer reservations system for Southwest's internal use, set to go into production in 1997, will also result in "multi-million dollar annual savings."

Southwest earlier released its third quarter report which showed net income down to $60.9 million, or $0.40 per share, from $67.7 million, or $0.45 per share, in the same period last year. Operating costs rose 6.5 percent to 7.52 cents per available seat mile.

Kelly said at least half the rise in costs was caused by a sharp rise in jet fuel prices and the federal fuel tax of 4.3 cents per gallon, but Southwest needs to refocus in order to remain the country's lowest-cost carrier.

"We had been very much focused on growth over the past five years. Here, in '96, '97 and '98 we will be very, very focused on performing as efficiently as we can and driving our units costs hopefully down," he said.
He said the effort includes productivity initiatives which have been, or will be, introduced in several operations groups, including maintenance.

"We still have a very, very wide cost advantage over the rest of the industry. We just dont want to lose that. We don't want to get complacent over where we are, so we have a number of initiatives underway to arrest this trend," Kelly said.

He said Southwest was also looking at ways of reducing the amount of fuel it burns. He said flying at lower speeds or carrying less weight are the only ways to reduce fuel burn but no decision has yet been made on what to do.

He stressed the cost-cutting program would not be allowed to undermine Southwest's safety standards. "Obviously, safety is the number one priority so in no way am I talking about taking measures that would impact safety," he said.
